notes: Fix: the catalogue's arduino-yun card lists only VIN, 3V3, GND, USB_MICRO, USB_A, ETHERNET and MICROSD. It has no 5V or A1 pin, but the tutorial's circuit and schematic need both. I added the new part type arduino-yun-headers. It is the same Yún board with its real header pins: A0-A5, 0-13, GND.1-3, 5V, 3.3V, VIN, IOREF, RESET, AREF, plus the USB, Ethernet and microSD connectors. yun1 now uses this type.
The black wire now goes to GND.1 instead of GND, to match the new type's port names. The image shows it on the first GND header pin.
The parts are otherwise the same as in step 1: yun1, bb1, tmp1, sd1 and three jumper wires (red, yellow, black).

Wiring follows the schematic and circuit image. Red goes from 5V to TMP36 pin 1 (+Vs). Yellow goes from A1 to pin 2 (Vout). Black goes from GND to pin 3 (GND). The TMP36 accepts 2.7-5.5 V, so 5V is within range.
The red wire sits on the header pin just right of the 3.3V label. That pin's own label is hidden by the wire, and the schematic shows 5V, so I used 5V.

Breadboard placement is my reading of the image. Each horizontal row of 5 holes is modelled as one column-bank strip: 10t for the +Vs row, 11t for the Vout row and 12t for the GND row. The sensor leg goes in hole a and the wire end in hole e of each strip.
The SD card is shown inserted in the Yún's microSD slot, as the circuit text says. It has no electrical edge because the tutorial gives no pin-level wiring for it.
The sketch's option of powering the sensor from A0/A2 is not built. The circuit image uses the 5V and GND header pins.
